[[File:お富士山古墳石棺（復元）.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Reproduction of a long chest-shaped Sarcophagus excavated from {{ill|Ofujiyama Kofun|ja|お富士山古墳}}<br />({{ill|National Museum of Japanese History|ca|Museu Nacional d'Història Japonesa|de|Nationalmuseum der japanischen Geschichte|es|Museo Nacional de Historia Japonesa|fa|موزه ملی تاریخ ژاپن|ff|National Museum of Japanese History|fr|Musée national d'histoire japonaise|hy|Ճապոնիայի պատմա-ազգագրական թանգարան|id|Museum Nasional Sejarah Jepang|ja|国立歴史民俗博物館|ko|국립역사민속박물관|ru|Национальный историко-этнографический музей Японии|tr|Ulusal Japon Tarihi Müzesi|uk|Національний історико-етнографічний музей Японії|zh|國立歷史民俗博物館|qid=Q3330690|lt=National Museum of Japanese History}})]]
'''Long chest-shaped Sarcophagus''' (長持形石棺, Nagamochigata Sekkan) is a type of composite {{ill|sekkan|ja|石棺|lt=Sarcophagus}} that appeared during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}.

== Overview ==
This type of box-type Sarcophagus is composed of six stone slabs: a base stone, two long side stones, two short side stones, and a lid stone. Its shape resembles a {{ill|Nagamochi|ja|長持|lt=Long chest}}, which gives it its name.

The short side stones and the upper part of the lid stone are rounded in a semicircular shape. Additionally, the lid stone, long side stones, and base stone have {{ill|rope attachment projections|ja|縄掛突起|qid=DELETED_QID}}.

These coffins are commonly found in large-scale kofun in the {{ill|Kinai|en|Kinai|qid=Q906708|lt=Kinai region}}, and in other areas, they are used for the tombs of local rulers. The Kinai examples are made from {{ill|rhyolitic welded tuff|ja|流紋岩質溶結凝灰岩|qid=DELETED_QID}}, also known as {{ill|Tatsuyama stone|ja|竜山石}}, sourced from the {{ill|Tatsuyama quarry|ja|竜山石採石遺跡}} in {{ill|Takasago, Hyōgo|en|Takasago, Hyōgo|qid=Q869037|lt=Takasago, Hyōgo}}.
